content:
Foldable screens often develop a visible crease after extended use, but Apple's Kate Bergeron says the foldable iPhone Duo's folding display features a replaceable protective layer to help mitigate this issue.

The "protective layer" on the iPhone Duo's folding display can be replaced over time to maintain its out-of-the-box condition

Following last month's launch of the iPhone Duo, Apple executives sat down for an interview to explain why the company has been so deliberate about improving durability and reducing the crease problem that plagues other foldables.

Part of that effort appears to be a unique design feature on the iPhone Duo that ensures it feels like the "first day out of the box" for years to come: a replaceable protective layer on the folding display.

Here's what Apple's VP of Hardware Engineering, Kate Bergeron, said during an interview with @angietutorials on TikTok:

Top comment from OrangeQuill

Now that I know they felt the need to do this, I'm even more worried about how this thing is going to age, hopefully they are just being overly cautious and don't charge an arm and a leg for repairs without AppleCare

You can watch the full clip on TikTok.

Apple references this "protective layer" in the iPhone Duo's AppleCare estimated repair cost sheet. According to Quinn Nelson, replacing the protective layer costs $19 with AppleCare. How much it costs without AppleCare has yet to be revealed.

So if you're worried about spending over $2,000 on an iPhone Duo only to find the crease becoming more pronounced over time, it sounds like Apple has a solution in place.

Have you been worried about the crease issue on the iPhone Duo? Let us know in the comments.
